learning_outcomes.text: The student solves a problem in a team where industrial devices and software link the automation world with the IT world.
The student can analyze the assignment, describe it, and formulate requirements/objectives.
The student consults with fellow students to achieve the intended end result.
The student tests and demonstrates the solution as a team.
The student documents the project as a team.
The student reports the solution as a team.
The student presents the solution as a team.
The student functions in a team.
The student verifies the realization against the established requirements.
The student can test the chosen devices and software and make them work together as one functional whole.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to industrial automation systems and software packages for industrial communication
Developing a basic assignment into specifications
Modular problem-solving to allow for testing of sub-systems
Testing whether the system meets the established specifications for both sub-solutions and the total solution
Demonstrating the solution and delivering documentation
Presenting the solution to the entire group of students
assessment_rules: The assignment is evaluated per team by the lecturer on five criteria: demonstration/operation of the solution (35%), structured problem solution (15%), test reports (15%), presentation (15%), and problem analysis/specifications (20%). A peer-factor is calculated for each individual student from a second peer assessment, which informs the individual score. There is no second examination opportunity and no partial transfers for this course.
bibliography: Handouts from the initiation (distributed via LMS)
Original device manuals (found on manufacturers' websites)
